newsitem.title: INDIA: Blast destroys India rail bridge, no one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Blast destroys India rail bridge, no one hurt.

text.p: Suspected tribal separatists blew up a railway bridge on Wednesday in the same region in northeast India where bomb explosions ripped through a passenger train earlier this week, police said.

Police said the latest explosion destroyed a small railway bridge about 160 km (100 miles) northeast of where dozens of train passengers were killed on Monday in explosions which wrecked the Brahmaputra Mail train.

No one was injured in Wednesday's explosion, which occurred early in the morning between Goreswar and Khoivabari towns, some 70 km (45 miles) west of Guwahati, the main city in Assam state, they said.

A police spokesman in Kokrajhar, near the site of Monday's blasts, said Bodo tribals fighting for a separate homeland were believed to have carried out both attacks, as well as an earlier one on Sunday.

The latest attack severed a key railway link to northeastern tea and oil-rich Assam. Monday's cut the main rail line between northeastern India and the rest of the country. The explosion on Sunday destroyed a bridge on a national highway, severing the main road link.
